comparison: Both evaluate claims C93-C95 about fitness costs and clinical implications of dedA mutations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of in vivo pathogenesis data. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 4 specifically noting that secondary mutations could overcome fitness disadvantages, which was not tested. Strong agreement on insufficient evidence.

Both evaluate the RplL ribosomal target mechanism (C58-C71). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting convergent evolution to rplL mutations and in vitro translation inhibition as compelling evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without methodological concerns, affirming the ribosomal targeting mechanism and novel binding site. Complete agreement.

Both address compound identification and BGC characterization (C14-C21). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, describing it as 'solid natural product discovery work' with standard characterization methods. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but Reviewer 2 questions the experimental design rationale (screening only 50 transposon mutants), though accepts the findings. Mostly aligned with minor methodological concerns from peers.

Both evaluate therapeutic lead claims (C12, C105-C106). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, stating claims are premature without pharmacokinetic, toxicity, or in vivo efficacy data. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting the critical gap of lacking in vivo validation in animal models. Strong agreement on insufficient evidence for therapeutic lead status.

Both evaluate cross-resistance data (C74-C78) supporting a novel binding site. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes the inference is indirect without direct binding studies or structural data. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting the cross-resistance data as sufficient evidence. OpenEval more cautious about mechanistic certainty.

Both address differential resistance patterns across Neisseria species (C81-C83). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes limited sample sizes and that the model remains inferential. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting the comparative findings as supporting the dual-mechanism model. Agreement on support with OpenEval noting data limitations.

Both address structural characterization of oxydifficidin (C22-C26). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting HRMS/NMR characterization is standard for natural product identification. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting analytical chemistry data through praise of methodological rigor. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate antimicrobial activity and narrow spectrum findings (C28, C30-C32, C101-C102). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting MIC data clearly demonstrates narrow spectrum activity and retention against resistant strains. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with all reviewers affirming this as the central finding with convincing evidence. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate DedA flippase mechanism (C37-C43). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting engineered deletion confirms phenotype and time-kill/morphology data provide mechanistic insight. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without methodological concerns, accepting the DedA uptake mechanism. Complete agreement.

Both address narrow spectrum activity claims (C27, C29, C31). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on MIC data in Figure 1c and Table 1. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting narrow spectrum as a key feature central to therapeutic appeal. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate DedA flippase mechanism with focus on accumulation assays (C50-C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes small sample sizes (n=2-3) and that direct flippase activity was not demonstrated. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without challenge to the accumulation data. OpenEval more cautious about mechanistic certainty.

Both evaluate the broader claim about reexamining old natural product sources (C13, C96). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting this is a hypothesis from a single example, not a demonstrated result. Peer Reviewer 3 implicitly supports the concept, acknowledging 'growing body of research to revisit potential antimicrobial agents.' Divergence: peers more receptive to the broader implication.

Both address low resistance frequency (C34-C35, C92). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for the genetic analysis including resistance frequency. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the finding without questioning methodology. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate novel ribosomal binding site claims (C79-C80, C104). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes inference is indirect without direct binding studies. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, affirming the novel binding site as well-characterized. OpenEval more cautious about level of proof.

Both evaluate bioinformatic survey of dedA diversity (C44). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the survey suggests dedA is essential in natural populations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewers 1 and 2 explicitly challenging the analysis as insufficient (only 220 isolates of unclear relationship). Significant disagreement: peers find evidence inadequate.

Both evaluate rplL diversity in natural populations (C62). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting rarity suggests fitness costs. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly stating 'genetic diversity of dedA and rplL in N. gonorrhoeae is still not clear' due to limited sample size. Significant disagreement: peers find evidence inadequate.

OpenEval evaluates background/contextual claims (C1-C9, C17, C97-C100) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and accurate framing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peers did not separately evaluate background claims.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims about ribosome structure and antibiotic targeting (C65-C67, C87-C90) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peers did not separately evaluate these contextual claims.

Peer reviewers evaluate genetic diversity analysis (C44, C62) as UNCERTAIN due to limited sample size (220 isolates). While OpenEval addresses these claims in R3 and R5 separately as SUPPORTED, the peer review groups them together and finds the combined analysis insufficient for the claims made.
